title: Level 2 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.0.title: 📋 Level 2 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.1.title: 🎯 Level 2 Key Takeaways
slides.1.points.0: 🏔️ Northern Italy: Trentino, Friuli, Liguria and Emilia-Romagna — each with a distinct identity
slides.1.points.1: 🌿 Trentino-Alto Adige: over 98% of production qualifies as DOC/DOCG
slides.1.points.2: 🍷 Friuli is celebrated for native white varieties: Tocai Friulano, Ribolla Gialla and others
slides.1.points.3: 🌊 Liguria's Vermentino carries a salty mineral character — a natural partner for seafood
slides.1.points.4: 🫧 Lambrusco is Emilia-Romagna's most iconic lightly sparkling red wine
slides.1.points.5: 🗺️ Central Italy: Marche's Verdicchio, Umbria's Sagrantino, Lazio's Frascati
slides.1.points.6: 🍇 Sagrantino di Montefalco has Italy's highest tannin content — minimum 37 months' ageing required
slides.1.points.7: ☀️ Southern Italy: Campania, Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria and Sardinia
slides.1.points.8: 🌋 Aglianico grows on volcanic soils — called 'the Nebbiolo of the South'
slides.1.points.9: 🔄 Primitivo and California Zinfandel are genetically identical — both originating in Croatia
slides.1.points.10: 👑 Nebbiolo → Barolo (traditional large-cask vs modern small-barrel debate)
slides.1.points.11: 🍇 Sangiovese → Brunello di Montalcino (minimum 5 years before release)
slides.1.points.12: 🍽️ Regional food pairing principle: local wine always pairs best with local food
slides.1.points.13: 💰 Top-estate Barolo Riserva holds its value best in the auction market
